Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 33669 of 2023

Applicant :- Abhay
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Dhiraj Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manisha Chaturvedi
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Ajeet Kumar Madhesiya, learned Brief Holder, for the State, apprised the Court that notice has
been served to the informant of the case on 28.7.2023.
2.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.
However, Ms. Manisha Chaturvedi, learned counsel appearing on behalf of High Court Legal Services Committee and the learned AGA, for the State, are present.

3. Heard Sri Dhiraj Kumar Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ajeet Kumar Madhesiya,
learned Brief Holder, for the State and Ms. Manisha Chaturvedi, learned counsel appearing on behalf of High Court Legal Services Committee.
4. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.142 of 2023, under Section 376 (2N) IPC and Section 5L/6 POCSO Act, Police Station Janakpuri, District Saharanpur during pendency of the trial.

sentences.text: 5 . FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and according to the FIR, applicant under the false promise of marriage sexually exploited the daughter of the informant.

6 . Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation of sexual exploitation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and even from both the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it reflects that she was consenting party.
7.
He further submtis that although as per school record the age of the prosecutrix is around 17 years but during investigation her ossification test was not conducted.

He next submits that from physical appearance prosecutrix appears to be a major girl aged about 18 years and at this stage merely on the basis of school record it cannot be said that she was below 18 years of age.
8.
He further submits that even as per school record prosecutrix is about17 years old, therefore, she has already attained puberty and she is almost at the verge of attaining the majority.
9. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 16.6.2023.

10. Per contra, learned Brief Holder as well as learned counsel for the High Court Legal Services Committee opposed the prayerfor bail and submitted that from the school record it appears that prosecutrix is around 17 years old girl and for the last about more than a year she was being sexually exploited by the applicant but both the learned counsels could not dispute the fact that during investigation ossification test of the prosecutrix was not conducted and it appears to be a case of love affair.

11. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.
12.

Although from the school record it reflects that at the time of lodgement of the FIR of the present matter, prosecutrix was around 17 years old and there is allegation against the applicant that he was sexually exploiting her under the false promise of marriage for the last more than a year but during investigation ossification test of the prosecutrix was not conducted and from the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. it reflects that she was having consent and present matter appears to be a case of love affair.
13. The law is settled that bail application should not be rejected either for punitive or preventives purposes.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

sentences.text:
Let the applicant-Abhay be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
Order Date :- 18.8.2023 SKM  Abhay vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106493335/
